summary: pp.1-12: Pages 1 to 12 of the MISO Large Load Working Group presentation outline MISO's proposed ±30 MW/min ramp rate limit for Computational Loads, its Tariff Section 37A.7 basis, technical derivation from regulation reserves, 1-minute aggregate PoW measurement methodology, and a comparison with SPP, ERCOT, ATC, AESO, and SOCO ramp proposals. | pp.13-17: Pages 13 through 17 of the MISO LLWG-2026-3 presentation cover qualitative ramp-limit applicability and exemptions for Computational Loads, exploratory non-compliance enforcement options, implementation milestones, stakeholder feedback questions, and contact information, with no explicit numeric power-variation limits.

constraints.snippet: The ±30 MW/min ramp limit (up and down) will be assessed every 1 minute across the aggregate net demand, inclusive of eligible generation, across a Computational Load’s applicable PoWs
constraints.notes: Applies up and down to Computational Loads; assessed every 1 minute across aggregate net demand including eligible generation across applicable Points of Withdrawal.

constraints.snippet: The Computational Load must have an effective up and down ramp rate not exceeding the specified limit outlined in the Business Practices Manual for Large Load unless otherwise directed by the Balancing Authority, Reliability Coordinator, or Transmission Operator.
constraints.notes: Qualitative Tariff obligation; ramp limits are measured in aggregate across applicable Point(s) of Withdrawal during stable-state transition, including eligible generation or other ramp-smoothing resources.

constraints.snippet: MISO’s proposed ramp limit of 30 MW/minute is consistent with existing industry proposals
constraints.notes: Proposed MISO ramp limit stated as 30 MW/minute in industry comparison slide.

constraints.snippet: Summary: Restricting Computation Load up/down movement at 30MW/min bounds a single facility’s 5-minute equivalent (150MW), preventing a single CL from using all of MISO’s regulation reserve and driving ACE violations under BAL-001-2.
constraints.notes: Derived as 15% of 1,000 MW maximum dynamic regulation reserves divided by the 5-minute UDS interval (150 MW/5 min = 30 MW over 1 minute); applies to Computational Loads agnostic of size.

constraints.snippet: Ramp rate is measured in aggregate across the applicable PoW(s), while allowing eligible generation to provide ramp smoothing
constraints.notes: Ramp rate measurement rule calculated over a 1-minute delta across applicable Point(s) of Withdrawal net of eligible local generation (GIA/ZGIA).

constraints.snippet: The ramp limit applies to normal operating conditions, including routine operational changes, unplanned interruptions, and restoration following outages.
constraints.source_section: MISO - Computational Load may deviate from ramp limit in some circumstances
constraints.notes: Qualitative applicability rule defining when the MISO Computational Load ramp limit applies.

constraints.snippet: The ramp limit does NOT apply: For automatic responses to system faults or disturbances required for equipment protection or fault ride-through performance. When Transmission Operator opens breaker(s) for shedding Load during Local Transmission Emergency. During a Computational Load customer-controlled "curtailment" during a Capacity Emergency or Local Transmission Emergency. Coordination would occur between MISO operations, Transmission Operator, and Computational Load with appropriate, stepped reductions.

constraints.notes: Qualitative exemptions from the ramp limit and coordination requirement for stepped reductions during emergency curtailments.
